questions.prompt: Walk through what happens in ww29 when an operator submits the batch form for three recipients on EMAIL and SMS with a raw subject and body and no template, from the form to the 200: how the operator is identified, which rules run at the boundary and which in the service, what is read before the transaction, and every row the transaction writes.

keyPoints.text: [w2] The form turns the datetime-local value into an ISO instant, sends subject and body only when no template is chosen, and the hook POSTs the payload to /api/notifications with credentials: "include".

[w3] Identity is an HS256-signed JWT in an HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax cookie: requireApiSession verifies the signature and takes userId and role from the token without reading the database, then checks notifications:create, and the service checks the same action again.

[w2] The zod schema bounds the batch (1 to 50 cuid recipients, at least one channel, a body of at most 5,000 characters), and its superRefine adds the cross-field rules: a template or a body, and a subject for EMAIL when there is no template. The service's input type is z.infer of that schema.

[w2] Before the transaction the service rejects a template with more than one channel (400), loads the recipients with their preferences and the template in parallel, and answers 404 if fewer users come back than ids were sent, or 400 if the template's channel differs.

[w3] One interactive transaction writes the batch, then per recipient a Notification with its merged personalisation values and one delivery per channel with subject and body already rendered, then one audit row, passing tx to every write. Here that is 11 rows: 1 batch, 3 notifications, 6 deliveries and 1 audit row.

[w3] Each delivery's fate is decided at write time: an opted-out channel or a missing phone number or push token gives SKIPPED with a reason; otherwise QUEUED with availableAt set to the scheduled or current time, moved to the end of quiet hours if it falls inside them.

[w2] Nothing is sent during the request: the route returns 200 with { batch }, the hook invalidates ["notifications"], and sending is left to the separate polling worker process, which picks up the QUEUED deliveries later.

questions.prompt: Explain what ww29 does with each of these batch requests, and which layer produces the outcome: the same recipient id listed twice; EMAIL listed twice in channels; a template together with EMAIL and SMS; a well-formed templateId that matches no template; a body using a {{firstName}} placeholder that nobody supplies; and a recipient with quiet hours 22 to 7 in a batch created at 23:30 server time. Then say what the operator sees in the UI when the boundary rejects a request.

keyPoints.text: [w2] A duplicated recipient id makes the IN lookup return one user for two ids, so the length check fails and the service answers 404 "One or more recipients were not found." before any write: a duplicate is reported as a missing recipient.

[w3] A duplicated channel passes the schema, which does not de-duplicate the array; the loop then writes a second EMAIL delivery for the first recipient, which violates @@unique([notificationId, channel]). The transaction rolls back and the caller gets a generic 500, because a Prisma error is neither an ApiError nor a ZodError.
[w1] A template with two channels is refused first, with a 400 from the service, before recipients or the template are read; the schema itself allows it.

[w2] A templateId that matches no row is not rejected: findUnique returns null, the channel check is skipped, and with the form sending subject and body as null, every delivery is stored with an empty body. The batch keeps the id only inside metadata, never in its templateId column.

[w2] An unsupplied placeholder renders as an empty string and is stored that way in the delivery's body; the values are the recipient's name, then the batch defaults, then per-recipient values (later ones win), and the form always sends featureName, callToAction and message as defaults.

[w3] Quiet hours read getHours(), the server's local hour, and preferences store bare hours with no time zone. 22 to 7 wraps midnight, so 23 is inside, and availableAt becomes 07:00 the next day on the server's clock, not the recipient's.

[w2] When the boundary rejects a request, the operator sees nothing useful: the 400 body says only "Validation failed." with the superRefine messages inside details, the hook throws body.error alone, and the page renders no mutation error, so the form simply stays filled.

questions.prompt: Defend or indict this claim about ww29's batch endpoint: "Batch creation is atomic and safe to retry: one transaction either writes the whole batch or nothing." Consider what the transaction does and does not cover, what a retry or a double submit does, how large the transaction can get, and what the session lets through. Say what you would change.

keyPoints.text: [w3] Atomic, yes: the batch, every notification and delivery, and the audit row share one interactive transaction, so a failure on the last delivery leaves no orphan batch. But recipients, preferences and the template were read before it opened, so an opt-out saved in between is not seen.

[w3] Not safe to retry: a batch has no idempotency key and no natural unique key, only a generated id, so a client that times out and retries creates a second batch, and the worker sends every message twice. The UI guards only against a second click while the mutation is pending.

[w2] Size: 50 recipients on all three channels is 1 + 50 + 150 + 1 = 202 inserts, each awaited in turn inside one interactive transaction. Prisma closes an interactive transaction after 5 s by default, so a slow database turns a full batch into a rolled-back 500.
[w2] Rendering at write time is a snapshot by design: each delivery stores its own rendered subject and body, so editing a template later never changes messages that are already queued.

[w2] The session is trusted for its whole seven-day life: role and user id come from the signed token and are never re-read, so a demoted or deactivated operator can keep creating batches until it expires, and logout only tells the browser to drop the cookie.

[w1] What can be defended: the boundary rules live in one schema whose inferred type the service uses, the channel enum is built from the Prisma enum with z.enum(NotificationChannel), and the permission is checked in both the route and the service.

[w2] Verdict: atomic but not retry-safe. Change: accept an Idempotency-Key, or a client-generated batch id, under a unique constraint and return the existing batch on replay; write notifications and deliveries with bulk inserts; and re-check the actor against the users table on writes.
